Live Grey Line Map

The grey line is where it is sunrise or sunset right now. Paths along it often bring unusual long-distance reception. The map updates every minute; your sunrise and sunset times are calculated from your location if you share it, or from your time zone otherwise.

How to use the grey line

Around your local sunrise and sunset, the absorbing D layer of the ionosphere is weak on the dark side, while the higher layers are still charged. Signals travelling along the terminator lose less energy, so distant stations can pop up for 30–60 minutes. Try the lower bands (90 m to 41 m) near your sunrise and sunset, aiming for stations that are also near their own sunrise or sunset. More in the grey line glossary entry.

Frequently asked questions

What is grey line propagation?

Enhanced long-distance reception along the sunrise/sunset line, where the absorbing D layer is weak but the reflecting layers are still ionised.

When should I listen on the grey line?

From about 30 minutes before to 30 minutes after your local sunrise or sunset.
